data.description:
BUILDPLAN.md T-03 (M0).

**Spike — the burst.** Minimal `axum` WebSocket room with 200 synthetic clients; the deadline burst in isolation; p95 write and reveal-fan-out measured on a deployed Fly machine. Go/no-go on D-A.

Criteria: AC-52, AC-53, AC-54, AC-41
Harness hooks: see EVALUATION.md rows for those IDs; `just test` is the inner loop (≤ 60 s).
Depends on (BUILDPLAN): T-01
BUILDPLAN notes: **Blocks M1.** If p95 fails, D-A option 2 is re-opened before any room code is written.

Orchestrator notes: Fly account is logged in (client confirmed 2026-09-20). The deploy itself runs outside the sandbox with the client's approval: prepare everything, then hand the exact `fly` commands to the Orchestrator. Attach p95 write and reveal fan-out numbers as an artifact; they are HC-0's burst evidence (F-2). Go/no-go on D-A is the client's call: report, do not decide.

Workflow mode: sub-agent-full. Terminal pre-merge status: review. PR base: origin/main.
Standing clauses: criteria outrank SPEC on behaviour, state, payloads and copy; SPEC outranks the prototype, which wins on visual detail only. Never write down what a program prints. Answer position is a uniform draw from the date, never balanced. Miri proves absence of UB on executed paths only. Colour is never the only signal. Code never causes horizontal page scroll. Never `git add -A`. Signing goes through 1Password: retry once, then escalate.

Plan: filled in by the delegator's plan phase.
data.title: Burst spike on Fly

data.body: READY PQ-3 CWD /Users/michellerojas/rust-nyc-pop-quiz-worktrees/burst-spike HEAD 2ab95e31b78ee48a7067dc47904e98b28baf3d37 BASE 2ab95e31b78ee48a7067dc47904e98b28baf3d37 MODE active

NOTE PQ-3 three divergences between the ticket body and the delegator brief, flagged not fixed.
1. PR base. Ticket body says 'PR base: origin/main'; the brief says base ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold (PR #8), press-ahead, retargeted to main once #8 merges. Taking the brief's side: it is the more specific and later instruction and it knows about #8. Rebasing onto origin/ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold @ 2ab95e31b78ee48a7067dc47904e98b28baf3d37.
2. Fly command ownership. Ticket body says 'prepare everything, then hand the exact fly commands to the Orchestrator'; the brief says run them here one at a time with the client approving in this tab. Taking the brief's side: the client watches this tab and the approval gate is already wired here (.claude/settings.json asks on Bash(fly *)). Every fly command will be shown before it runs.
3. Sandbox carve-out gap. The worktree .claude/settings.json carves out reads of .env.example only. Writes to $LATTICE_ROOT/.lattice/ are outside the sandbox allowlist, so every lattice write (comment, status, attach, plan) fails with PermissionError on .lattice/locks/ and has to run with the sandbox bypassed. Same for git fetch/push over SSH. Working, but worth adding to the carve-out for the rest of the fleet.

ORCHESTRATOR RULING: where the ticket text and your boot brief differ, the brief governs (it is later and knows about PR #8). PR base is ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold until #8 merges; fly, push and PR commands run in your tab with the client's approval. The worktree .claude/settings.json now also allows sandboxed writes to /Users/michellerojas/rust-nyc-pop-quiz/.lattice, so lattice commands should no longer need the bypass; git fetch/push over SSH still do.

ORCHESTRATOR: PR #8 merged to main at 0742d35 (merge commit; your base commit 2ab95e3 is its second parent). From now on: rebase onto origin/main (git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main; it should be a no-op or trivial), and open your PR against main, not ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold. Drop the 'Based on #8' line from the PR body.

PLAN PQ-3 planned then in_progress. Plan and the authoritative review-resolutions block are on the plan file. Review: 0 Critical, 3 Major, 6 Minor; all nine triaged.
Base changed, verified not assumed: PR #8 merged as 0742d35 with 2ab95e3 as its ancestor, origin/ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold is deleted on the remote, and git diff origin/main...HEAD was empty. The brief's own retarget condition has already fired, so the press-ahead stack is spent: rebased onto origin/main @ 0742d35, PR will open --base main, and the 'Based on #8' line is dropped. This also retires divergence 1 from my earlier comment - ticket body and brief now agree.
Three review findings changed the measurement, the rest were wording or accepted gaps:
- AC-54 now runs BOTH burst shapes as headline (uniform over 2s, and spike - all 200 inside the last 50ms), three cycles each, and the headline is the worst cycle p95 across both. Only the easier shape drove the exit code before, so the harder one could never affect the D-A go/no-go. Both satisfy SPEC 9's '200 writes inside 2 s' literally.
- The AC-53 worked example was arithmetically wrong: churn is 1+(i mod 3) over 200 clients = 399 writes, +200 burst = 599, not ~800. Rank is 570, not 760. p95_rank is now computed from the actual n at runtime and printed, never hardcoded. Also pinned explicitly: post-close refusal acks are never in AC-53's population, enforced by an assertion.
- AC-52 gains a per-session fingerprint (XOR over sessions of a hash of session/letter/seq) because applied_seq_sum is a pooled sum a two-session swap could cancel. Still no per-session answer is exposed.
Also: CI ranks now floor/ceil outward to [183,197] rather than rounding inward, which fires 'marginal' more often not less; 1Password signing procedure written into the implement phase; serde/serde_json corrected to 'already transitive'.
Known gap for T-21, not fixable here: required-features = spike is what guarantees the 60s budget and is also why neither test nor test-full ever type-checks the spike bins. justfile and CI are not on this ticket's cleared list. Mitigation is cargo check/test --features spike, named in room/README.md and run before the PR.

DONE PQ-3 PR https://github.com/mrojas54/rust-nyc-pop-quiz/pull/11 HEAD ea858eceaa421f32777a4b21c179fba960f6a9e2 BASE 0742d3578726e3e0486c7b3793c6bb934e3e8579 (origin/main; see deviation 1) test-warm 0.33s CI just test SUCCESS, just test-full SUCCESS on ea858ec. PR OPEN, MERGEABLE, body verified stored byte-identical.

RESULT, worst of three valid runs on one shared-cpu-1x/256MB machine in ewr, from the laptop: AC-54 92.38ms (<500), AC-53 63.49ms (<500), AC-41 117.47ms (<=2000), AC-52 exact in all three. None marginal. Headroom 5.4x / 7.9x / 17x. The go/no-go on D-A is the client's call; nothing here decides it.

deviations:
1. PR base is main, not ai-c11-cc/repo-scaffold. PR #8 merged as 0742d35 before implementation began and the scaffold branch was deleted, so the brief's own retarget condition had already fired. Rebased onto origin/main; no 'Based on #8' line.
2. fly commands ran in this tab with client approval, per the brief, not handed to the Orchestrator per the ticket body. Every command was shown before it ran.
3. Four measured runs, not three. Run 1 connected 199/200, so it is invalid (exit 2); it is committed and not quoted. Run 4 was taken with the same binary as the third valid run.
4. AC-54 runs two burst shapes (uniform over 2s, and all 200 in the last 50ms), and the worst cycle across both is the headline. That is stricter than SPEC 9's floor (plan-review M-3). The spike shape set the headline in every valid run.
5. The spike server has no auth, as the ticket says. After a security review, resource bounds were added: reveal pad clamped to 64KiB, new session ids capped, inbound frames capped at 64KiB.
6. Code-review Minor 3 deferred: some plan-schema diagnostic fields are absent from the report (control_rtt_ms, clock_offset_ms_median, server vm fields). None feeds pass/fail, and join_rtt_ms already carries the network floor (p50 38-48ms). The round-2 reviewer accepted the deferral.
7. The TLS-off and half-load diagnostics are not committed. TLS-off passed 200/200. Half-load was invalid at 0/100, likely for the same cause as run 1.
8. The committed reports are schema /1, from the code at c5e020f. The current binary writes /2; the changes are summary fields only (quotable, AC-54 marginal, nullable pass on invalid runs). room/spike/reports/README.md documents the difference.
9. ea858ec (the mechanical fixes after the round-2 PASS-WITH-NITS on c693574) was not re-reviewed, per the brief's rule for mechanical fixes.

notes:
- FOR T-09, which holds room state in memory: fly deploy created a SECOND machine 'for high availability' despite min_machines_running=1. For the real room that splits state across two machines. Deploy with --ha=false or scale count 1. fly launch also overwrote fly.spike.toml and stripped every comment; check git diff after launch.
- FOR T-04b (join and capacity): likely, not proven, that ghost sessions behind the Fly proxy caused both invalid runs. Session ids repeat per run, and the spike decrements 'present' only when it notices a close. Tie capacity to session lifetime, or back-to-back rooms will refuse joins. It failed safe here: capacity gates join only.
- FOR T-21: (a) required-features=spike keeps just test in budget, and also means neither test nor test-full type-checks the spike bins; by-hand gate: cd room && cargo check --features spike && cargo test --features spike (32 pass). (b) The harness records that a join failed but not why; add the reason. (c) Consider renaming the spike feature when the client is promoted.
- FLY TRIAL: the org has no payment method, so Fly stops every machine after 5 minutes. Runs fit inside 5-minute windows; a full run takes about 55s. HC-0's re-run needs either a card at https://fly.io/trial or the same windowing.
- END STATE: app rustnyc-popquiz-spike intact at rustnyc-popquiz-spike.fly.dev, both machines stopped, i.e. scaled to zero. Not destroyed. Destroy command, for the client to decide: fly apps destroy rustnyc-popquiz-spike --yes
- COST (ESTIMATE, from fly.io/docs/about/pricing, read 2026-09-22): at scale-to-zero Fly charges only rootfs, $0.15 per GB per 30 days, with no CPU or RAM charge. Two stopped machines from a 24MB image come to well under $0.05/month. The shared IPv4 and the IPv6 are free, and no dedicated IPv4 was allocated (that would be $2/mo). Running: $2.32/month per shared-cpu-1x 256MB, from the page's table, whose row is not ewr-specific. The page does not say whether a trial org with no card is billed at all.
- SANDBOX: needed a bypass for fly (~/.fly), git over SSH, the uv cache (just test's pipeline half cannot run sandboxed) and the c11 socket. .lattice writes were carved out mid-run.

ORCHESTRATOR: PRs #9 (shared web layer) and #10 (bank format) merged to main: 36250b3 then 238146e. main now carries web/shared/** and the bank format. Their branches were auto-deleted. Rebase onto origin/main (git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main), base your PR on main, and read web/shared/typemodel.js from main rather than the old branch.
